system.name: NGC 3603
system.description: One of the most massive young stellar clusters in the Milky Way, 22,000 light-years away in the Carina arm. Its dense core contains some of the most massive stars known, including the WN6h giant NGC 3603-A1 — one of the heaviest stars ever measured at over 100 solar masses.

ngc3603.name: NGC 3603-A1
ngc3603.description: A WN6h Wolf-Rayet supergiant of roughly 116 solar masses — one of the most massive stars ever measured. It sits at the heart of the densely packed NGC 3603 star cluster, which formed in a single burst of star formation and contains the highest concentration of massive stars in the Milky Way.
ngc3603.funFact: The NGC 3603 cluster forms new stars so rapidly that its core luminosity rivals that of 30 Doradus in the Large Magellanic Cloud — Hubble images revealed hundreds of massive stars crammed into a region just a few light-years across.
